posts.name: Jeysie
posts.cooked:
Ulf316:

hence they might prioritize the tool that makes their game playable to sell more physical copies of Oblivaeon.

If we assume iOS has similar download numbers to Android, that means there’s around 2K people who own Sidekick.

The OA kickstarter had about 10K backers.

So even among physical owners, the people who use Sidekick are a minority, and thus it is likely not a major driving force behind people buying OblivAeon.

That’s also without noting the fact that there’s plenty of people like myself who own both Sidekick and Season 2. And basically I can still play physical OA without help and use the OA heroes and environments with help, but I can’t yet play digital OA content at all, so my own personal priority of the two is still “finish digital OA”.

I’d also note that GTG is also a small business that has at times talked about the logistics of having to prioritize projects based on what keeps the lights on, so I am going to guess they’re not going to tell Handelabra to use a different business model from themselves. C&A have also expressed time and time again they’re just happy whenever there’s new fans of Sentinels and generally don’t seem to place physical-owning fans in a tier over the digital-owning ones.

I empathize with your frustration since as I noted plenty of us own both things and are equally looking forward to Sidekick being finished as we are to the digital app. But you also made your case and were given I feel a polite answer that I recognize is not what you wanted to hear but is also an answer that makes sense logistically for them to give.

So I just am noting that if your goal is to try to change that answer via prodding the community and GTG to get mad at Handelabra and demand they focus on a 2K-selling product over a 250K-selling product–with the latter product being again one even those of us who own Sidekick, also own the other one too–I just don’t feel that you’re going to succeed there.

Ulf316:

I was hoping both the company and fans of the paper game would be concerned as I am and exert pressure

And what I’ve been trying to point out/warn you about is that the company and fans of the paper game are also looking forward to the digital version as well, and there’s also a very large quantity of digital-only fans on top of it, who are all thus more likely to be concerned with and exerting pressure about the digital version, all of which is something Handelabra also has to listen to.

“We all knew this” more or less because much of the online Sentinels community is fans of both GTG and Handelabra and so we keep tabs on both. If you go to Reddit you’re likely to find people more concerned with when the digital version is coming out (there was a thread about the topic literally just the other day in fact) and Steam and the fan Discord are definitely both primarily concerned with the digital version.

I tried to give you polite nudges but that seems to have not worked, so I guess I have to be a little more blunt: The reason you’re not finding much traction is because even the people who own Sidekick here generally either also own the digital version and care more about that being done first, or they just understand that the pressure exerted from a quarter million people is a lot heavier than the pressure exerted from a few thousand people.

Not to mention, to loop back to my initial post in this thread, a lot of the problems they have to solve UI and tracking-wise are likely to be very similar for both Sidekick and the full app, so it’s likely even if they put full resources on it you still wouldn’t have that much of a difference in ETA anyway simply because they’d have to solve much the same problems either way regardless.
